skills.name: Segments & midpoints
skills.wrong_turn: The midpoint splits the segment in half: if AM = 7, then AB = 14, not 7. Solve for x, then give the length asked for.
skills.rule: Segment addition: if B is between A and C, then AB+BC=AC.

skills.name: Angles & bisectors
skills.wrong_turn: A bisector makes two halves, each half the whole: if m∠ABC = 80°, each half is 40°, not 80°.
skills.rule: Angle addition: if D is inside ∠ABC, then m∠ABD+m∠DBC=m∠ABC.

skills.name: Angle pair theorems
skills.wrong_turn: Vertical angles are opposite each other across the crossing, not side by side. Side-by-side angles there are supplementary, not equal.
skills.rule: Vertical angles are congruent. Angles supplementary (or complementary) to the same angle are congruent.

skills.name: Parallel line theorems
skills.wrong_turn: These angle facts need parallel lines. If the lines aren't parallel, corresponding angles need not be equal.
skills.rule: Parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding and alternate angles are congruent; same-side interior angles are supplementary.

skills.name: Proving lines parallel
skills.wrong_turn: Don't use the theorem to prove its converse. To show lines are parallel, reason from the angles, never from "since the lines are parallel".
skills.rule: Congruent corresponding or alternate interior angles, or supplementary same-side interior angles, make lines parallel.

skills.name: Perpendicular lines

steps.c: distance from a point to a line

skills.wrong_turn: Distance to a line is along the perpendicular, not along any segment. From (0, 5) to y = 1 it's 4, though (3, 1) is 5 away.
skills.rule: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles; the distance from a point to a line is measured along the perpendicular.
